result:
I found and fixed 10 rules whose output didn't match their docstrings. A script that computes the expected price from each docstring now matches all 150 rules (`mismatching rules: []`). It checked a grid of quantities around each threshold against several unit prices, not every possible input.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 35 | Cap applied to the amount before the percentage (`min((qty-50)*unit, 30000) * 12 // 100`) | Compute the discount, then cap it |
| 93, 102 | Cap applied to the price, not the discount (`min(base, cap) * pct // 100`) | Compute the discount, then cap it |
| 45, 57, 115 | `round()`, which can round up, instead of flooring to the won | Use floor division `// 100` (done with one sed command) |
| 66 | 3% instead of the documented 2% | Changed to 2% |
| 83 | 8% instead of the documented 7% | Changed to 7% |
| 105 | Docstring says marginal, code applied the discount to every unit | Discount only units above 30 |
| 107 | Docstring says whole, code discounted only units above 5 | Discount every unit |

Rules 39 and 43 also had the wrong threshold in code (`>= 6` instead of 5, `>= 21` instead of 20). For marginal rules the discount at exactly the threshold is 0 anyway, so prices don't change. I fixed them anyway so the code matches the docstrings.

The other 138 rules matched as they were. My comparison script and a backup of the original file are in the scratchpad, not the project.

STATUS: DONE
